**PhonePe launches UPI service without internet**

PhonePe launched **UPI 123Pay on 31 August 2026** becoming the first major TPAP to bring internet free UPI payments to India’s **200M+ feature phone users**. Powered by SMS technology it supports P2P transfers QR merchant payments balance and transaction checks. 

It comes Pre bundled on Nokia, HMD ,Lava and ITEL devices. 

PhonePe said the rollout is built on a proprietary technology stack developed specifically for enabling UPI payments on feature phones.
**SMS-based architecture for low-connectivity regions **PhonePe UPI 123Pay runs on an SMS-based architecture designed to keep transactions functional even in areas with limited 2G network coverage.

**Iran's IRGC has released footage of the recent ballistic missile and drone launches towards the American King Hussein and Muwaffaq Salti air bases in Jordan in retaliation for the strike on Iran’s Larak Island.**


Iran's IRGC says it launched a combined ballistic missile and drone attack against the American King Hussein and Muwaffaq Salti air bases in Jordan in retaliation for the strike on Iran’s Larak Island.

The group says it targeted technical and maintenance infrastructure as well as areas housing fighter jets at both bases, claiming to have caused heavy damage.

The IRGC warned that further attacks would not weaken Iran’s control over the Strait of Hormuz and said any additional strikes would be met with an "even more crushing response."

**"One Nation, One Time"**:

The Central Government of India has notified rules to make IST(Indian Standard Time) as common time reference.

The Government of India has notified the **Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026** __mandating Indian Standard Time (IST) as the single reference for legal, administrative, commercial and other official purposes across the country__.

These rules will come into force 180 days after their publication in the Official Gazette, giving government departments, businesses, and institutions time to align their systems.

**Court Ruling Details** -

**Core Decision:** The court upheld the previous rejection of India's trademark application, affirming that Basmati is a shared geographical indication. 

**Equal Rights:** The decision recognizes that Basmati rice is grown in both Pakistan and India, giving traders from both countries a legitimate right to use the term. 

**No Monopoly:** No single national authority can claim exclusive ownership or monopoly over the word "Basmati" in the Australian market.

Govt is planning to levy charges on every UPI payment in the future 🙂

Center has introduced a new bill in the #Parliament on (04.08.2026) 

**10. The Taxation and Others Laws** (Amendment) **Bill, 2026:** It removes the strict "**zero-fee**" mandate on digital payments to allow a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on select business transactions.

The legislation amends __Section 10A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007__ giving the government the legal authority to structure merchant fees in the future.

For 6 years, a line in Indian law said nobody could charge you for a UPI payment.

On Thursday the Lok Sabha voted to delete that line.

There was no discussion. It went through on a voice vote while the House was in protest over something else.

The line is Section 10A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007. It barred banks and payment system providers from charging, directly or indirectly, on the electronic payment modes listed in the tax law.

The amendment does not impose a fee on UPI.

It deletes the reference to the tax law and replaces it with a line saying the central government may notify which payment modes stay free.

That is the whole event. Not a new charge. A new pen.

Removing the free guarantee used to require a vote in both Houses.

Narrowing it now requires a notification signed by the executive.

Same outcome available, one tenth the friction, and no debate on the record

Its just a matter of time before it's passed in Rajya Sabha too. #Economy #Policy

FCRA: Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act 

➜ Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA) is the law that governs how Indian individuals, associations, NGOs, trusts and companies may receive and use money, securities or articles sent to them from a source outside India. It is administered by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)

➜ FCRA does three things: 

💠 It identifies who may accept foreign contributions, and on what conditions.

💠 It specifies how that money must be received, accounted for, and reported.

💠 It restricts a narrow, defined set of foreign-funded activities that could affect India’s sovereignty, security or public order.

➜ FCRA establishes a clear, rules-based process for every organisation that wishes to receive foreign contributions in India

Excavations at Sarthe Rongphar village in Karbi Anglong, Assam have uncovered ancient stone sculptures and inscriptions dating likely to the 10th-12th centuries, shedding new light on the state’s heritage. 

Finds include dancing figures, deities, Shiva lingams, temple fragments and a carving of Lord Ganesha, with many artefacts now preserved at museums in Hojai and Diphu. 

Locals link them to the Mahabharata era, but experts believe they are from the Ahom period, highlighting the broader Phuloni-Dokmoka-Howraghat region’s archaeological importance. #Heritage

Excavations at Malayadipatti near Karivalamvanthanallur in Tamil Nadu’s Tenkasi district show continuous human settlement from the Stone Age to the Sangam era. 

Archaeologists have found microlithic tools, an 8.7m Sangam-era brick structure, iron tools, beads, pottery, shell bangles, and a red-slipped burial pot with painted peacocks, suggesting the site was an organized industrial and trade center on an ancient east-west route, not just a habitation. #Heritage

The funding will support projects under Urban Challenge Fund, Bhubaneswar-Cuttack-Puri-Paradeep Economic Region, and Mukhyamantri Sahari Vikas Yojana, with flexible 25-year repayment and Centre-state cost sharing, to modernise cities and develop new urban growth centres. #Economy #Infra

IKEA plans to invest close to ₹11,000 crore in India by 2030 to speed up store expansion, local sourcing, and hiring, with a target to open 25 large and small-format stores. It is also investing over ₹7,500 crore via Ingka Group for new Ingka Centres in Gurugram and Noida, and reported 6% sales growth in FY25 to ₹1,860 crore, but expects double-digit growth this year. #MakeinIndia

India’s new Index of Service Production (ISP) showed 14 of 19 sectors posted double-digit growth in April, with accommodation and food services leading at 37.2% YoY, followed by retail trade at 30.8% and administrative/support services at 28.7%. The monthly index, launched by MoSPI with base 2024-25, covers 60% of the formal services sector and CEA V Anantha Nageswaran called it a "real achievement" signaling a strong start to FY26 for India’s services #economy.
